title: Graph Search & Query Planning
description: Study neighborhood expansion, path queries and evidence chains, hybrid text and graph retrieval, and query classification and routing. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Neighborhood expansion
lessons.description: Define allowed relation types and a traversal budget.
lessons.conceptOverview: Start from resolved query entities and expand along relevant relation types with depth and size limits. Unbounded expansion increases irrelevant context and can expose unrelated data.
lessons.whyItMatters: Traversal should follow the query's relation needs.

lessons.title: Path queries and evidence chains
lessons.description: Explain what each edge supports and where the proposed conclusion exceeds the evidence.
lessons.conceptOverview: A multi-hop answer requires support for every edge in the path and correct composition of relation meanings. A connected path does not automatically establish causation or the relation asked by the user.
lessons.whyItMatters: Connectivity alone does not justify arbitrary relational conclusions.

lessons.title: Hybrid text and graph retrieval
lessons.description: Design a retrieval flow that fetches supporting passages after graph expansion.
lessons.conceptOverview: Text retrieval finds detailed source passages; graph retrieval supplies explicit relations and neighborhoods. Combine candidates and preserve source evidence because a graph summary may omit important qualifications.
lessons.whyItMatters: Graph structure should be paired with source-level evidence.

lessons.title: Query classification and routing
lessons.description: Compare a local-neighborhood plan with a corpus-summary plan.
lessons.conceptOverview: Local entity questions and broad corpus questions require different retrieval strategies. Route based on information needs and allow fallback when entity resolution or graph coverage is insufficient.
lessons.whyItMatters: Retrieval strategy should match question scope.
